title: RBI likely intervenes, anchoring rupee in face of global ructions, traders say - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
State-run banks were ⁠spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf ‌of the RBI. | Photo Credit: bl-online Administrator

The Reserve Bank of India likely intervened ‌in the foreign ​exchange market ⁠on Monday, five traders told Reuters, to protect ‌the rupee against pressure arising ‌from uncertainty ‌over ⁠the US-Iran ⁠war and corporate hedging flows.

The rupee was little ​changed on ‌the day at 95.6425 per dollar, clinging to a ‌narrow range in ​early trading.

State-run banks were ⁠spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf ‌of the RBI, traders said.

Traders reckon that robust inflows ‌under policy measures ​to strengthen India's balance of payments ⁠have bolstered the ⁠RBI's ability to support the rupee ‌via interventions.
